domains.note: Strongest commercial signal in the corpus: OD043 is affiliated with TuSimple and OD047 ties false-positive reduction to production-vehicle safety.
Deployment claims are concrete and hardware-measured, from OD098 stating detectors are deployed in industry on drone and robotics edge devices to OD114 benchmarking an iPhone 12 with CoreML.
OD056 describes already-running urban camera use cases such as free-parking search and OD008 targets surveillance commercialization, but no paper names a shipped surveillance product.
OD098 reports industry deployment of detectors on robotics edge devices while most other papers such as OD017 name robotic manipulation only as a target application.
These papers motivate real-time detection only in the abstract as in OD052 and OD109, and deployment evidence appears only once a paper names a vertical.
OD091 and OD094 provide deployment-ready detector suites aimed at industry requirements, yet the claims stop at industry scenarios as in OD096 rather than named customers.
OD079 asserts detection is already deployed in medical image analysis while the other papers such as OD110 only name applications with no product or clinical deployment.
Product ties are visible in OD007's Megvii affiliation and OD016's production-scale face attribute classifier, but no paper claims a shipped face-detection product.
Six papers chase crowd benchmarks such as OD069 on CrowdHuman and OD024 on CityPersons, and none reports a deployed crowded-pedestrian system.
OD009 reports detectors deployed in products such as Google Photos and Pinterest Visual Search, extending the Pinterest adoption OD001 records earlier.
Every aerial paper evaluates on academic sets such as OD027 on remote-sensing imagery and OD042 on HRSC2016 ship detection, with no commercial or deployed remote-sensing product.
Evidence is product and lab affiliation rather than deployment, with OD044's author at Amazon Rekognition and OD045 produced in collaboration with Megvii.
The four papers only suggest uses - OD111 proposes screen parsing and OD079 suggests language-directed search - and none reports a deployed document or screen-parsing product.
OD079 cites fruit detection and OD116 crop-health UAV monitoring as application areas, but neither reports a deployed agricultural product.
OD012, OD049 and OD081 treat sports, pose and egocentric cues purely as evaluation settings, and none reports a deployed system.

gaps.title: Crowd and pedestrian detection has no deployment trail
gaps.detail: Six papers build on crowd benchmarks - OD069 on CrowdHuman, OD024 on CityPersons and re-annotated Caltech - and name video surveillance and autonomous driving only as future applications, yet no deployment claim in the corpus concerns crowded-pedestrian systems.

gaps.title: Aerial and satellite detection stays benchmark-bound
gaps.detail: All five aerial papers evaluate on academic sets - OD027 on remote-sensing imagery, OD042 on HRSC2016 ship detection, OD098 on DOTA - and none reports a commercial or deployed remote-sensing product.

gaps.title: Medical imaging output outruns its adoption evidence
gaps.detail: Nine papers name medical applications - OD082 on medical imaging advances, OD110 on organ and tumor delineation - but the only deployment-flavoured statement is OD079's generic claim that detection systems are already deployed in medical image analysis, with no product or hospital named.

gaps.title: Challenge wins drive adoption but are not an indexed domain
gaps.detail: Deployment-adjacent claims track competition success - OD009 reports the winning 2016 COCO entry and OD022 first place in the COCO 2017 challenge - while the academic application index treats competition-winning systems only as two scattered strings (OD001, OD010).

gaps.title: Defense guidance appears as an application without academic coverage
gaps.detail: Applications name military visual guidance and defense funding - OD032 lists military visual guidance, OD036 is DARPA-funded, OD099 flags drone target recognition - but the corpus has no deployment claim for defense uses and no paper develops detection specifically for them.

gaps.title: Query and set-prediction detectors stay benchmark-bound
gaps.detail: The transformer-query family (25 papers) and set-prediction family (18) dominate recent accuracy tables, yet OD107 has to remove DETR's grid_sample operator to make deployment work and OD106 names computation and deployment cost as the barrier to practical use of such detectors.

gaps.title: Heatmap and corner detectors never clear the real-time bar
gaps.detail: The keypoint-based (6 papers) and gaussian-heatmap (5 papers) families need dense high-resolution output maps plus heavyweight post-processing, and OD051 states outright that the corner-based original is too slow for video applications.

lowAdoption.reason: Its 25 papers mostly report datacenter-GPU accuracy, and OD107 must strip DETR's grid_sample operator to escape the deployment constraints it names as typical of this family.

The corpus's own deployment papers work around operator-heavy models: OD087 drops deformable convolution and Matrix NMS for hardware support and OD099 builds from simple validated operators so deployment devices do not miss support.
Hungarian-matching set losses add heavy, unstable training, and only OD096 and OD108 place a set-prediction detector in a deployment context, both as benchmark scenarios rather than shipped products.
OD051 states the corner-based original's latency is too slow for video, and none of the six keypoint-based papers reports a deployment.
Heatmap detectors must run dense high-resolution output maps with heavyweight post-processing, and none of their five corpus papers carries a deployment claim.
Multi-resolution pyramid testing multiplies inference cost per image, and none of its four papers appears in a deployment claim in the corpus.
